classification_signals: Abstract states 'two examples, one positive and the other negative, are discussed as field work for a better understanding of psychological architecture.'
The paper provides detailed descriptions and analyses of two specific architectural projects (Pruitt-Igoe and Samanbahce Quarter) to illustrate theoretical points.

The methodology involves presenting these cases and interpreting their outcomes through the lens of existing psychological and architectural literature, rather than collecting new empirical data or conducting statistical analyses.
title: Architecture Psychology

findings.antecedent: architectural designs that do not consider human psychology and thermal comfort
findings.consequent: lack of sense of belonging to the house
findings.quote: people of all ages are not obeying the 'stay at home, stay healthy' warnings... this is due to the fact that people do not feel a sense of belonging to the house they live in.

findings.antecedent: sensory stimuli (visual, auditory, olfactory, somatosensory)
findings.consequent: activation of hippocampus, formation of new memories, environmental mapping
findings.quote: particular cells in the human brain hippocampus responsible from the location, is activated by any sensory stimulus... and it plays critical role in the formation of new memories and environmental mappping [2].

findings.antecedent: objects in spatial connections with each other
findings.consequent: positive development of individual's sense of direction, feeling of belonging
findings.quote: objects are in spatial connections with each other is related to the positive development of the individual's sense of direction and this is one of the primary factors for the individual to feel the sense of belonging.

findings.antecedent: difficulty in finding direction in places
findings.consequent: occurrence of negative emotions, sense of being lost
findings.quote: Places in which people have difficulty in finding their direction is closely associated with occurrence of negative emotions in human psychology, in terms of sense of being lost in particular [3].

findings.antecedent: architectural façades and interior designs
findings.consequent: trace in human psychology
findings.quote: starting from details in the architecture façades, interior designs, too, leave a trace in human psychology [4].

findings.antecedent: danger signals received in the living environment
findings.consequent: increased intensity of individuals' stressful lives, deteriorating psychologies (decreased energy, blocked creativity, exhaustion of hopes, weakening of personalities)
findings.quote: Danger signals received in the living environment increase the intensity of individuals' stressful lives and it manifests itself with psychologies that deteriorate...

findings.antecedent: architecture
findings.consequent: unearths creativity in the spirit of a person, emotional sense of creativity products
findings.quote: Architecture, already, is a notion that unearths the creativity in the spirit of a person and the products of this creativity in the emotional sense [6].

findings.antecedent: inadequate exposure to sunlight
findings.consequent: increased frequency of depression cases
findings.quote: Scientific studies have shown that there is a significant association between the frequency of depression cases and inadequate exposure to sunlight [7].

findings.antecedent: predominant apartment designs (1+1 and 2+1) in today's property market
findings.consequent: failure to meet people's needs for disintegration, differentiation, and private spaces in relationships
findings.quote: predominant apartments in the style of 1 bedroom + living room and 2 bedrooms + living room (1+1 and 2+1) are far from designs to meet people's needs for disintegration and differentiation in their relationships with others and creating private spaces.

findings.antecedent: lack of private space in spatial design (e.g., crowded open offices)
findings.consequent: negativity in human psychology and relationships, difficulty in establishing in-depth relationships
findings.quote: The private space notion in the spatial design that reflects in human psychology and relationships as negativity manifests itself in the office designs... The crowded communities... do not reflect positively in terms of establishing and maintaining an in-depth relationship...

findings.antecedent: feeling of belonging in one's environment
findings.consequent: happiness
findings.quote: it is of great importance for people to feel belonging in order to be happy in their environment [13].

findings.antecedent: green color tone (symbolizing peace, tranquility, abundance, renewal)
findings.consequent: more positive impressions on human psychology
findings.quote: the green color tone, which is the symbol of concepts such as peace, tranquility, abundance, renewal, leaves more positive impressions on human psychology [13].

findings.antecedent: feeling of security risk, uneasiness, fear, and unhappiness in the living environment
findings.consequent: alienation from the environment, estrangement from sense of belonging
findings.quote: The feeling of security risk, uneasiness, fear, and unhappiness in the living environment leads to alienation from there and being estranged from the sense of belonging [13].

findings.antecedent: alienation from the living environment
findings.consequent: negative effects on interactions of people living in the same environment
findings.quote: This alienation, on the other hand, negatively affects the interactions of people living in the same environment with each other [13].

findings.antecedent: dwellings and workplaces constructed ignoring human psychology
findings.consequent: disturbance of social 'communal' lives
findings.quote: In short, dwellings and even workplaces constructed ignoring human psychology disturb social 'communal' lives.

findings.antecedent: disturbed social order (e.g., due to ignoring human psychology in design)
findings.consequent: psychological problems, alienation from the city
findings.quote: When people's order is disturbed, psychological problems begin, and in this case, the person starts not to see himself/herself as a part of the city anymore, and thus, he/she alienates from the city he/she lives.

findings.antecedent: Pruitt-Igoe design (small apartments, skip-stop elevators, communal corridors, poor ventilation, no AC)
findings.consequent: attraction of muggers (safety risk), poor thermal comfort, abandonment, deterioration, crime-infested neighborhood, architectural failure
findings.quote: The floors where elevators stopped were equipped with larger communal corridors... attracted muggers. In addition, ventilation was poor... Pruitt-Igoe was nearly abandoned and had deteriorated into a decaying, dangerous, crime-infested neighborhood...

findings.antecedent: lack of maintenance and funding for upkeep (Pruitt-Igoe)
findings.consequent: deterioration of the project
findings.quote: residents cite a lack of maintenance almost from the very beginning... as being a primary cause of the deterioration of the project.

findings.antecedent: thoughtful public housing design (e.g., Samanbahce Quarter)
findings.consequent: residents can live without leaving social life, feeling a sense of belonging, even with small residential sizes
findings.quote: public housing can be built where the residents can live without leaving the social life by feeling a sense of belonging, even if the net residential sizes are small.

findings.antecedent: mutual opening of doors (Samanbahce houses)
findings.consequent: air circulation, natural air conditioning (thermal comfort)
findings.quote: Thanks to the mutual opening of the doors, air circulation occurs in the entrance hall and natural air conditioning is achieved.

findings.antecedent: specific shutter design (lower fixed, upper openable) in Samanbahce houses
findings.consequent: privacy for residents, air circulation
findings.quote: passers-by cannot see the inside of the room, and because the upper part is openable, air circulation is ensured by being opposite the window opening out to the courtyard.

findings.antecedent: collecting water-related indoor spaces in the same place (Samanbahce houses)
findings.consequent: prevention of facial paralysis due to temperature difference after hot bath
findings.quote: if a person who comes out of a hot bath during the wintertime tries to go directly to the living room or bedroom, facial paralysis may occur due to the temperature difference.

findings.antecedent: use of modern insulation materials instead of loam (soil) on roofs during restoration (Samanbahce houses)
findings.consequent: negative effect on natural air conditioning and thermal comfort
findings.quote: modern insulation materials are used instead of loam (soil) on roofs during the restoration works... and that this event negatively affects natural air conditioning, in other words, thermal comfort.

findings.antecedent: lack of window opening to the courtyard and single-wing door/window (Samanbahce houses, later additions)
findings.consequent: blocked air circulation, affected natural climate
findings.quote: The fact that the room was not built with a window opening to the courtyard affected the natural climate, because air circulation is blocked.

findings.antecedent: courtyards with water (Samanbahce houses)
findings.consequent: evaporative cooling, contribution to natural climate
findings.quote: This is due fact that in the evaporative cooling process water absorbs relatively large amount of heat [24].

findings.antecedent: streets without vehicle traffic (Samanbahce Quarter)
findings.consequent: open spaces for visual neighborhood relationships
findings.quote: Streets without vehicle traffic are open spaces where neighborhood relationships are visual.

findings.antecedent: housing projects designed with fast production and cheap materials, ignoring human needs for privacy and differentiation
findings.consequent: prevention of feeling a sense of belonging, mental depression
findings.quote: This situation prevents people from feeling a sense of belonging to the place they live in and leads people to be mentally depressed.

limitations: The paper does not explicitly state limitations of its own case study analysis or methodology.
minimum_safe_summary: This paper argues that architectural design significantly impacts human psychology, well-being, and social life. It highlights that ignoring human psychological needs, thermal comfort, and spatial differentiation in design leads to negative outcomes like a lack of belonging, increased stress, and mental depression. Conversely, designs that consider these factors, even with small residential sizes, can foster social life and a sense of belonging. The paper illustrates these points through two case studies: the failed Pruitt-Igoe complex, attributed to architectural flaws and poor maintenance, and the successful Samanbahce Quarter houses, which demonstrate effective natural air conditioning, privacy, and community-fostering layouts. The primary limitation is the absence of explicit methodological limitations for the case study analysis itself.
